A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E2M research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite extensive expansion in v4.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original image-reconstruction, noisy half-moon, tabular classification/density-estimation, and synthetic-density experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original experiments and add quantitative noise analyses and non-tensor comparisons. Appendix B.7.1 also reports Gaussian-mixture fitting results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 adds recomputation of forward TT contractions after updating the cores and before constructing P, correcting the earlier procedure. The central double-bound algorithm and CP/Tucker/TT mixture models remain; combining the two E steps was already present in v3.

E1.justification: V4 adds evaluated continuous Gaussian-mixture fitting (Figure 2, Appendix B.7.1) and a noise-corrupted CarEvaluation scenario (Figure 14b). It removes v3's known CP/TT synthetic-density experiments (Figure 11 left, Appendix D.1.4). The main tabular benchmarks, SIPI House, and half-moon coverage remain.

E2.justification: V4 Table 8 adds a tree-structured Bayesian network (BaysNet), HMM, and DiscreteFlow evaluated against EMCPB and E2MCPTTB, substantially extending comparison beyond tensor methods. The original BM, KLTT, CNMF, EMCP, and gradient-optimizer comparators remain.

E3.justification: New noise experiments evaluate reconstruction against clean and contaminated distributions using five divergences and different ranks; new Gaussian-mixture and non-tensor comparisons introduce additional evaluation settings. Appendix D.1.3 changes the reported generalization evaluation from Ttrain to Ttest without establishing reruns. Existing data splits and SIPI rank settings remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds quantitative alpha/noise sensitivity studies, a small-rank control investigating overfitting, noisy real-data analysis (Figures 7 and 14), and iteration-wise objective-change analysis (Figure 5b–c). It removes the synthetic sample-size recovery study. The background-term and mixture-component ablations already existed in v3.

E5.justification: Both versions already report five random initializations and dispersion. V4 adds Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction for classification comparisons against BM, KLTT, CNMF, and EMCP. This adds statistical testing without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The retained tensor benchmark and ablation values match, including reported E2MCPTTB mean accuracy 0.776. V4 adds non-tensor scores, Gaussian-mixture fits, longer optimization traces, and quantitative noise findings; Figure 7 reports optimal alpha near 0.3 under high noise versus 0.7 under low noise for Jeffreys divergence. Synthetic sample-size recovery results disappear.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects Theorem 1's monotonicity direction and boundedness argument; the bound definition also changes J's sign. V4 adds a gradient-complexity derivation (Appendix B.3) and Gaussian-mixture update derivations (B.7.1). The existing Tucker/TT closed-form derivations are largely retained.

C1.justification: The main double-bound and closed-form mixture-learning contributions remain. V4 additionally claims a demonstrated connection to Daudel et al.'s auxiliary-function framework in the introduction, extending v3's prospective suggestion that E2M could serve as an alternative.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly states that objective convergence does not guarantee iterate or stationary-point convergence and identifies missing generalization theory. It adds alpha-selection guidance, interprets noise as regularization using the small-rank control, and discusses feature-order and latent-variable limitations in the expanded comparisons.

D1.justification: V4 supplies explicit softmax parameterization, Gaussian-mixture generation parameters, and software, search spaces, and training budgets for BaysNet, HMM, and DiscreteFlow. Much original tuning, hardware, and code-access information remains. The expanded softmax explanation alone does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and Appendix D.1.4 substantially expand positioning against neural density estimators, discrete flows, probabilistic tensor models, and tensor-completion methods, with numerous new citations. The already-cited Daudel et al. (2023b) receives a direct comparison identifying identical Gaussian-mixture updates despite different bounds.

P1.justification: The introduction, problem setup, method explanations, and results narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Dedicated subsections expand sparsity remarks, alpha selection, many-body modeling, and proof explanations. V4 also adds an ethical statement, acknowledgments, and journal front matter.

P2.justification: V4 expands Figure 1, adds Gaussian-mixture and normalization diagrams, quantitative noise plots, and notation, abbreviation, complexity, and baseline tables. Figure 5 reorganizes optimization and background results. Existing illustrations and tables are relocated or redisplayed, alongside substantial caption, axis, and layout changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces v3's contradictory increasing/upper-bound convergence argument with non-increasing/lower-bound reasoning and clarifies the guarantee's limits. Quantitative robustness tests, comparisons with additional model families, and expanded reproducibility guidance substantially strengthen evaluation and interpretation. These gains outweigh removal of the synthetic sample-size validation, although notation and dataset-count inconsistencies remain.
